quote: APA § 9.4(c) provides that the cap in § 9.4(a) and the basket in § 9.4(b) "shall not apply to any claim under Section 9.2(a)." Section 9.2(a) is the representation-and-warranty indemnity—the single most common source of post-closing claims. As drafted, Seller's exposure for a rep/warranty breach is uncapped. ... If a Buyer claim for a non-fundamental rep breach ... exceeds $1,840,000, Marrowind is personally liable for the excess with no cap. ... (c) Exceptions. The limitations set forth in Section 9.4(a) and Section 9.4(b) shall not apply to (i) any claim arising from fraud or (ii) any claim based on a breach of a Fundamental Representation.
reason: The memo meets all three parts of the criterion. First, it identifies the problem: the § 9.4(c) carve-out removes the 10% cap for all § 9.2(a) claims, covering every rep and warranty and not only fundamental ones. Second, it explains why this matters to Marrowind: the company is exposed to uncapped liability above the $1,840,000 escrow. Third, it recommends narrowing the carve-out to fraud and Fundamental Representations. The memo does not add the ledger's suggested Purchase Price cap on those claims, but the criterion does not require that.
